project.name: cert-manager
project.description: cert-manager adds certificates and certificate issuers as resource types in Kubernetes clusters, and simplifies obtaining, renewing, and using those certificates from sources including ACME (Let's Encrypt), HashiCorp Vault, Venafi, and local in-cluster issuers.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Auto-generated root Makefile that bootstraps the cert-manager build: sets host OS/arch and git version variables, defines the _bin/artifacts directories, a clean target, and includes the repository-specific and shared make modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses .SECONDEXPANSION and last-moment variable evaluation so module-provided dependency variables resolve late; shared logic lives in make/_shared and is cloned via klone.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project README describing what cert-manager does, its supported issuers, documentation and installation pointers, development and contribution guidance, Go module compatibility caveats, and security reporting instructions.

nodes.name: RELEASE.md
nodes.summary: Release documentation covering the release schedule, links to the detailed release process, and the artifacts produced per release: container images, Helm chart, and binaries.

nodes.name: ROADMAP.md
nodes.summary: Minimal roadmap stub noting that the project roadmap has moved to the cert-manager community repository.

nodes.name: SECURITY.md
nodes.summary: Security policy stub directing vulnerability reporters to the cert-manager organisation security document.

nodes.name: SECURITY_CONTACTS.md
nodes.summary: Stub document pointing to the cert-manager organisation security contacts list used for private vulnerability reports.

nodes.name: USERS.md
nodes.summary: Stub document redirecting to the cert-manager organisation users list maintained in the community repository.

nodes.name: go.mod
nodes.summary: Go module definition for github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager on Go 1.25, pinning Kubernetes, controller-runtime, cloud provider SDKs, Vault, Venafi, and other dependencies required by the certificate issuance components.
nodes.languageNotes: Split into direct and indirect require blocks with `// indirect` markers; a comment reserves the top of the file for replace directives.

nodes.name: go.sum
nodes.summary: Generated Go checksum lock file recording module hashes for every direct and transitive dependency in the cert-manager module graph.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated by the Go toolchain; must not be hand-edited.

nodes.name: klone.yaml
nodes.summary: Klone manifest declaring which cert-manager makefile-modules (boilerplate, go, help, licenses, repository-base, tools, helm) are cloned into make/_shared and at which pinned commit, driving the root Makefile includes.

nodes.name: Chart.template.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm chart metadata template for the cert-manager chart, defining the chart name, description, keywords, maintainers, Artifact Hub annotations, and minimum Kubernetes version.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains {{IS_PRERELEASE}} placeholders and placeholder version/appVersion fields that the release tooling substitutes when generating the final Chart.yaml.

nodes.name: README.template.md
nodes.summary: Helm chart README combining installation, upgrade, and uninstall instructions with a complete auto-generated reference for every chart value (236 headings across global, controller, webhook, cainjector, and ACME solver settings).
nodes.languageNotes: The Configuration section is marked AUTO-GENERATED and is produced by helm-tool from the +docs annotations embedded in values.yaml; {{RELEASE_VERSION}} is substituted at release time.

nodes.name: signkey_annotation.txt
nodes.summary: Two-line metadata file holding the fingerprint and download URL of the GPG key used to sign cert-manager Helm chart releases, read by the build to annotate the generated Chart.yaml.
nodes.languageNotes: Consumed verbatim by make/manifests.mk via a read loop and written as an Artifact Hub signature-key annotation on the generated chart.

nodes.name: values.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) validating the cert-manager Helm chart values, using 252 nested $defs entries to constrain every top-level value and each component's image, resource, scheduling, and security settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Built around a single helm-values root definition with additionalProperties: false and per-component $ref chains such as #/$defs/helm-values.cainjector.

nodes.name: values.yaml
nodes.summary: Default values for the cert-manager Helm chart, configuring the controller, webhook, cainjector, ACME solver, startup API check, CRDs, RBAC, monitoring, and shared global scheduling and image-pull settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily documented with +docs:section and +docs:property comment annotations that drive README generation and the values schema.

nodes.name: NOTES.txt
nodes.summary: Helm post-install notes displayed after installing the cert-manager chart, warning about the deprecated installCRDs value and the new private key rotation default, then pointing users to Issuer and ingress-shim documentation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Go template conditionals so the deprecation warning only appears when installCRDs is set.

nodes.name: cainjector-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Renders an optional ConfigMap holding the cainjector configuration file, defaulting apiVersion and kind to cainjector.config.cert-manager.io/v1alpha1 CAInjectorConfiguration.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutates the values map in-template using Helm's set function to inject API defaults before serializing with toYaml.

nodes.name: cainjector-deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Defines the cainjector Deployment, wiring replicas, leader election, feature gates, optional config volume, Prometheus metrics port, security context, scheduling constraints, and image pull secrets for the CA injector component.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of named templates (image, labels, cainjector.fullname) with nindent to compose nested YAML blocks conditionally.

nodes.name: cainjector-poddisruptionbudget.yaml
nodes.summary: Optional PodDisruptionBudget for cainjector pods that applies minAvailable or maxUnavailable from values and defaults to minAvailable 1 when neither is configured.

nodes.name: cainjector-psp-clusterrole.yaml
nodes.summary: ClusterRole granting the cainjector service account use of its dedicated PodSecurityPolicy when the deprecated podSecurityPolicy feature is enabled.

nodes.name: cainjector-psp-clusterrolebinding.yaml
nodes.summary: ClusterRoleBinding that binds the cainjector PodSecurityPolicy ClusterRole to the cainjector service account in the release namespace.

nodes.name: cainjector-psp.yaml
nodes.summary: Legacy policy/v1beta1 PodSecurityPolicy restricting cainjector to unprivileged containers, fixed UID/GID 1000, no host namespaces, and a minimal set of volume types.
nodes.languageNotes: PodSecurityPolicy was removed in Kubernetes 1.25, so this template is gated behind global.podSecurityPolicy.enabled.

nodes.name: cainjector-rbac.yaml
nodes.summary: Full RBAC set for cainjector: cluster-wide read and update access to certificates, secrets, webhook configurations, APIServices and CRDs, plus leader-election Role and RoleBinding in the configured namespace.
nodes.languageNotes: Bundles multiple YAML documents separated by --- inside a single Helm template.

nodes.name: cainjector-service.yaml
nodes.summary: ClusterIP Service exposing the cainjector Prometheus metrics port 9402, rendered only when monitoring is enabled without a PodMonitor.

nodes.name: cainjector-serviceaccount.yaml
nodes.summary: Creates the cainjector ServiceAccount with configurable token automounting, annotations, labels, and global image pull secrets.

nodes.name: controller-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Renders an optional ConfigMap containing the controller configuration, defaulting apiVersion and kind to controller.config.cert-manager.io/v1alpha1 ControllerConfiguration.

nodes.name: crd-acme.cert-manager.io_challenges.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced ACME Challenge resource, including the full OpenAPI v3 schema for solver types such as HTTP-01 and DNS-01.
nodes.languageNotes: A 3k-line generated OpenAPI schema preserved with Helm conditionals and optional helm.sh/resource-policy annotations.

nodes.name: crd-acme.cert-manager.io_orders.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced ACME Order resource, describing certificate identifiers, issuer references, and authorization status.

nodes.name: crd-cert-manager.io_certificaterequests.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced CertificateRequest resource, capturing CSR data, issuer reference, requested duration, and issued certificate status.

nodes.name: crd-cert-manager.io_certificates.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced Certificate resource, defining secretName, DNS names, issuers, keystore options, private key rotation policy, and renewal status.

nodes.name: crd-cert-manager.io_clusterissuers.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the cluster-scoped ClusterIssuer resource, containing the shared IssuerSpec and IssuerStatus schemas for ACME, CA, Vault, Venafi and self-signed issuers.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the Issuer schema but at cluster scope, making the OpenAPI body one of the largest templates in the chart.

nodes.name: crd-cert-manager.io_issuers.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced Issuer resource, defining issuer backends (ACME, CA, Vault, Venafi, self-signed) and their status conditions.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Defines the main cert-manager controller Deployment, configuring replicas, leader election, feature gates, optional config volume, metrics endpoint, security context, and pod scheduling.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses quoted comparison tricks in Helm conditionals so that a log level or revision limit of 0 is still honored.

nodes.name: extras-objects.yaml
nodes.summary: Generic escape hatch that renders every entry of .Values.extraObjects through Helm's tpl function so users can inject arbitrary additional Kubernetes manifests into the release.
nodes.languageNotes: The tpl call evaluates each extra object as a template with the chart's root context, allowing user-supplied values to be interpolated.

nodes.name: networkpolicy-egress.yaml
nodes.summary: Optional egress NetworkPolicy for the webhook pods, allowing operators to restrict outbound traffic from webhook components via values.

nodes.name: networkpolicy-webhooks.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template rendering a NetworkPolicy that restricts ingress traffic to the cert-manager webhook pods, with ingress rules supplied from .Values.webhook.networkPolicy.ingress.
nodes.languageNotes: Guarded by a Helm `if` on webhook.networkPolicy.enabled and uses `toYaml | nindent` to inject user-supplied ingress rules.

nodes.name: poddisruptionbudget.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating a PodDisruptionBudget for the cert-manager controller, defaulting to minAvailable: 1 unless the user sets minAvailable or maxUnavailable.

nodes.name: podmonitor.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template producing a Prometheus Operator PodMonitor that scrapes the cainjector, controller, and webhook pods on the http-metrics port, failing the render if ServiceMonitor is enabled at the same time.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `fail` to enforce mutual exclusivity between the PodMonitor and ServiceMonitor chart options.

nodes.name: psp-clusterrole.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template defining a ClusterRole that grants the `use` verb on the cert-manager PodSecurityPolicy resource by name.

nodes.name: psp-clusterrolebinding.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template binding the cert-manager PSP ClusterRole to the controller ServiceAccount so the controller may use the PodSecurityPolicy.

nodes.name: psp.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template defining a restrictive PodSecurityPolicy for cert-manager controller pods, with non-privileged containers, fixed UID/GID 1000, and a whitelist of volume types.

nodes.name: rbac.yaml
nodes.summary: Large Helm template rendering the controller's full RBAC surface: leader-election and token-request Roles/RoleBindings plus ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings for issuers, clusterissuers, certificates, orders, challenges, ingress-shim, approvals, certificate signing requests, and aggregated view/edit roles.
nodes.languageNotes: Emits roughly two dozen multi-document YAML resources from a single template, guarded by global.rbac.create and serviceAccount.create conditionals.

nodes.name: service.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating a ClusterIP Service exposing the controller's Prometheus metrics port 9402 for ServiceMonitor scraping, rendered only when Prometheus is enabled without PodMonitor.

nodes.name: serviceaccount.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating the cert-manager controller ServiceAccount with configurable image pull secrets, automount settings, annotations, and labels.

nodes.name: servicemonitor.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template rendering a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor that scrapes cert-manager component endpoints by target port, with a guard preventing simultaneous PodMonitor enablement.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-job.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template defining the post-install startup API check Job, which runs the cert-manager image with `check api --wait` to verify the API is serving before the release is considered healthy.
nodes.languageNotes: Merges global and component nodeSelector maps with the Helm `merge` function before rendering.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-psp-clusterrole.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template granting the `use` verb on the startup API check PodSecurityPolicy through a dedicated ClusterRole.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-psp-clusterrolebinding.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template binding the startup API check PSP ClusterRole to the startupapicheck ServiceAccount.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-psp.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template defining a PodSecurityPolicy for the startup API check Job pods, permitting only projected and secret volumes with fixed UID/GID 1000.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-rbac.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating a Role and RoleBinding that let the startup API check ServiceAccount create CertificateRequests during the post-install verification.

nodes.name: startupapicheck-serviceaccount.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating the startup API check ServiceAccount with configurable annotations, labels, automount token, and image pull secrets.

nodes.name: webhook-config.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template packaging the webhook's WebhookConfiguration values into a ConfigMap under config.yaml, defaulting apiVersion and kind before serializing with toYaml.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutates the values map in place with Helm's `set` before serializing it into the ConfigMap data field.

nodes.name: webhook-deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template for the cert-manager webhook Deployment, wiring replicas, security context, feature gates, dynamic-serving CA secret flags, health and metrics ports, and the mounted webhook configuration ConfigMap.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive conditional templating covers hostNetwork/dnsPolicy, Prometheus scrape annotations, and configurable secure-port and healthz-port overrides.

nodes.name: webhook-mutating-webhook.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template registering the MutatingWebhookConfiguration that intercepts CREATE operations on cert-manager CertificateRequests and routes them to the webhook service's /mutate path.
nodes.languageNotes: Annotated with cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from-secret so cainjector populates the CA bundle from the webhook CA Secret.

nodes.name: webhook-poddisruptionbudget.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template creating a PodDisruptionBudget for webhook pods, defaulting to minAvailable: 1 unless the user overrides availability settings.

nodes.name: webhook-psp-clusterrole.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm-templated ClusterRole granting the cert-manager webhook permission to 'use' its PodSecurityPolicy, rendered only when global.podSecurityPolicy.enabled is true.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML manifest interleaved with Go template directives, so it is only valid after Helm rendering.

nodes.name: webhook-psp-clusterrolebinding.yaml
nodes.summary: ClusterRoleBinding that binds the webhook PodSecurityPolicy ClusterRole to the webhook ServiceAccount, gated on the podSecurityPolicy feature flag.

nodes.name: webhook-psp.yaml
nodes.summary: PodSecurityPolicy for the cert-manager webhook pods, disabling privileged mode and privilege escalation while restricting volumes, host access, and runAs/seccomp/AppArmor profiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the deprecated policy/v1beta1 PSP API behind a Helm values flag; hostNetwork and securePort are driven by .Values.webhook.

nodes.name: webhook-rbac.yaml
nodes.summary: Bundles all webhook RBAC objects: a namespaced Role/RoleBinding for reading and updating dynamic serving-certificate Secrets and a ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding for creating SubjectAccessReviews.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains four documents in one file separated by '---', with resourceNames scoped to the CA Secret and conditional metrics-TLS Secret access.

nodes.name: webhook-service.yaml
nodes.summary: Service exposing the webhook over HTTPS on port 443 and optionally a Prometheus metrics port, with configurable service type, IP families, load balancer IP, annotations, and labels.

nodes.name: webhook-serviceaccount.yaml
nodes.summary: ServiceAccount for the webhook pods with configurable token automounting, annotations, labels, and global image pull secrets, created only when webhook.serviceAccount.create is set.

nodes.name: webhook-validating-webhook.yaml
nodes.summary: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration registering webhook.cert-manager.io for CREATE/UPDATE on cert-manager.io and acme.cert-manager.io resources, with CA injection, Equivalent match policy, and a service or URL client config.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the cert-manager cainjector annotation to inject the CA bundle from a Secret into the webhook configuration.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Short reference note explaining that the CRD YAML files in deploy/crds are source material used to build the officially supported deployment manifests (e.g. the Helm chart) and are not intended for direct use by end users.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses GitHub blockquote syntax for the end-user warning admonition.

nodes.name: acme.cert-manager.io_challenges.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the ACME Challenge resource (challenges.acme.cert-manager.io, v1) defining the full OpenAPI schema for in-flight ACME challenge validation, including solver configuration, DNS-01/HTTP-01 status fields, and challenge state.
nodes.languageNotes: Large generated structural schema (3,476 lines) with deeply nested per-solver properties and x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields free-form blocks.

nodes.name: acme.cert-manager.io_orders.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the ACME Order resource (orders.acme.cert-manager.io, v1) describing the schema of an ACME order, its authorizations, identifiers, and certificate request references.
nodes.languageNotes: Compact generated CRD with a single served/storage version and nested status subresource schema.

nodes.name: cert-manager.io_certificaterequests.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the CertificateRequest resource (certificaterequests.cert-manager.io, v1), defining the CSR payload, issuer reference, and issued certificate response schema.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes shortNames for kubectl and a status subresource carrying base64-encoded certificate data.

nodes.name: cert-manager.io_certificates.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the Certificate resource (certificates.cert-manager.io, v1) covering desired certificate specs such as secretName, dnsNames, issuers, keystores, and renewal policy along with status conditions.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested keystore and secret template schemas show heavy use of x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields for user-supplied labels and annotations.

nodes.name: cert-manager.io_clusterissuers.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the ClusterIssuer resource (clusterissuers.cert-manager.io, v1), defining the cluster-scoped issuer schema with ACME, CA, Vault, Venafi, and self-signed issuer configurations.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest CRD in the batch (4,068 lines) mirroring the namespaced Issuer schema with deeply nested per-issuer-type configuration and solver selectors.

nodes.name: cert-manager.io_issuers.yaml
nodes.summary: CustomResourceDefinition for the namespaced Issuer resource (issuers.cert-manager.io, v1), defining issuer backend configuration for ACME, CA, Vault, Venafi, and self-signed issuers plus their status conditions.
nodes.languageNotes: Nearly identical in size and structure to the ClusterIssuer CRD, differing mainly in scope and metadata.

nodes.name: 01-namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Namespace manifest that creates the cert-manager namespace, prefixed with 01 so it is applied before other deployment resources.
nodes.languageNotes: Starts with a YAML document separator so it can be concatenated with other manifests.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains that the static deployment manifests moved to being generated from the official Helm chart and published as GitHub release assets from v0.8 onward.

nodes.name: helm-values.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm values overlay for the cert-manager chart that pins the release name, sets small CPU/memory requests for the controller and ingress shim, and enables the webhook.

nodes.name: namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Minimal Kubernetes Namespace manifest declaring the cert-manager namespace for deployment manifests.

nodes.name: 20190708.certificate-request-crd.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal introducing the CertificateRequest CRD as the hand-off point between certificate controllers and issuers, covering API fields, approval/denial conditions, RBAC scope, ACME and issuing controller behaviour, and graduation criteria.

nodes.name: 20191218-security-context-deprecation.md
nodes.summary: Design note describing how to deprecate the Helm chart's boolean securityContext.enabled in favour of an arbitrary securityContext block, including pseudo-code precedence rules and eight backwards-compatibility test cases.

nodes.name: 20200326.extensible-certificate-controller.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for refactoring the Certificate controller into composable keymanager, requestmanager, and issuing components, with new API fields that make issuance and private key handling extensible.

nodes.name: 20210203.certificate-request-identity.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal adding user identity (username, UID, groups, extra attributes) to CertificateRequest and propagating it so issuers can make authorisation decisions and embed identity in issued certificates.

nodes.name: 20210209.certificates.k8s.io-adoption.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for adopting the upstream certificates.k8s.io CertificateSigningRequest API and signer model, covering third-party interoperability, security implications, field mapping, and the migration path away from the CertificateRequest CRD.

nodes.name: 20220118.certificate-issuance-exponential-backoff.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal introducing exponential backoff for failed certificate issuance attempts, defining new status fields and worked examples for automatic and manually triggered reissuance.

nodes.name: 20220118.server-side-apply.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal to migrate cert-manager controllers from update/patch semantics to server-side apply, covering field manager naming, conflict resolution, field deletion, and feature-gate rollout.

nodes.name: 20220614-timeouts.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal to increase controller and issuer operation timeouts, remove intermediate middleware timeouts, and raise ACME HTTP client timeouts so slow external issuers no longer fail spuriously.

nodes.name: 20221205-memory-management.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for cutting cert-manager memory consumption by caching partial object metadata and applying transform functions to strip Secret data before objects enter informer caches, with benchmarks and alternatives analysis.

nodes.name: 20230302.gomod.md
nodes.summary: Design document describing the split of the cert-manager repository into multiple Go modules (one per binary, separate test modules, and a pkg/apis module) to reduce dependency churn and simplify patching.

nodes.name: 20230601.gateway-route-hostnames.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for inferring TLS hostnames from Gateway API Route objects so cert-manager can populate Certificate DNS names automatically from Gateway/HTTPRoute resources.

nodes.name: 20240122.scarf.md
nodes.summary: Short proposal to adopt Scarf.sh for container image download analytics and to decouple cert-manager images from the Jetstack-branded Quay repository as part of CNCF vendor-neutrality work.

nodes.name: 20240206.helm-resource-policy.md
nodes.summary: Proposal to add the helm.sh/resource-policy: keep annotation to cert-manager CRDs and standardise CRD upgrade options in the Helm chart so uninstalling the chart does not delete CRDs and user data.

nodes.name: 20240518.push-to-multiple-registries.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal enabling release tooling to publish cert-manager image artifacts to multiple container registries, covering mirroring strategy, credentials, failure handling, and rollout criteria.

nodes.name: 20240625.push-charts-to-oci.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for publishing cert-manager Helm charts to an OCI registry in addition to the traditional chart repository, including signing, risks, and graduation criteria.

nodes.name: acme-orders-challenges-crd.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal introducing first-class ACME Order and Challenge CRDs so order flow state is no longer hidden inside the Certificate status, along with the required API types, order and challenge controllers, and refactoring plan.

nodes.name: template.md
nodes.summary: Reusable design-document template adapted from the Kubernetes KEP template, providing standard sections such as summary, motivation, proposal, design details, test plan, and production readiness for new cert-manager proposals.

nodes.name: artifact-metadata.template.json
nodes.summary: Template for release artifact metadata JSON, with TODO placeholders for artifact name, sha256 digest, OS, and architecture filled in by release tooling.

nodes.name: boilerplate-go.txt
nodes.summary: Apache 2.0 license header template in Go comment syntax, passed to Kubernetes code generators via --go-header-file so generated files carry the cert-manager copyright notice.

nodes.name: boilerplate-sh.txt
nodes.summary: Apache 2.0 license header template in shell comment syntax, prepended to generated shell files such as the kind image list.

nodes.name: boilerplate-yaml.txt
nodes.summary: Apache 2.0 license header template in YAML comment syntax with a YEAR placeholder, used when stamping generated YAML manifests.

nodes.name: concat-yaml.sh
nodes.summary: Concatenates a list of YAML files into a single multi-document stream, inserting `---` separators between files and failing on missing files or unsupported `%YAML` directives.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on bash `set -eu -o pipefail` and positional-argument shifting for a streaming file loop; no functions are defined.

nodes.name: k8s-codegen.sh
nodes.summary: Drives all Kubernetes code generation for cert-manager, invoking deepcopy, client, lister, informer, defaulter, conversion, OpenAPI, and apply-configuration generators over the versioned and internal API packages.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash array parameter expansion (`${arr[@]/#/$module_name/}`) is used to prefix package paths; each generator binary is injected as a positional argument.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Deletes generated files matching a given name under a path, returning early when the directory does not exist.

nodes.name: gen-openapi-acme
nodes.summary: Generates the OpenAPI definitions for the ACME webhook API into pkg/acme/webhook/openapi, cleaning stale output and writing a report file first.

nodes.name: gen-openapi-client
nodes.summary: Generates the client OpenAPI definitions for the public cert-manager API packages alongside required Kubernetes and Gateway API dependencies.

nodes.name: gen-deepcopy
nodes.summary: Regenerates zz_generated.deepcopy.go files for every internal and external API package, bounded to the cert-manager module.

nodes.name: gen-applyconfigurations
nodes.summary: Generates client apply-configuration types for the public API using a locally generated OpenAPI schema, working around upstream fake-clientset limitations.

nodes.name: gen-clientsets
nodes.summary: Generates the versioned typed clientset for the cert-manager and ACME APIs into pkg/client/clientset.

nodes.name: gen-listers
nodes.summary: Generates typed listers for the cert-manager and ACME APIs into pkg/client/listers.

nodes.name: gen-informers
nodes.summary: Generates shared informers for the cert-manager and ACME APIs, wiring them to the generated clientset and listers.

nodes.name: gen-defaulters
nodes.summary: Generates defaulting functions for internal API types used by the mutating webhook, supplying extra peer package directories.

nodes.name: gen-conversions
nodes.summary: Generates conversion functions between internal and external API versions for the conversion webhook, with extra peer package directories configured.

nodes.name: latest-base-images.sh
nodes.summary: Resolves the latest crane digests for distroless static and dynamic base images across all supported architectures and writes them as Makefile variables to make/base_images.mk.
nodes.languageNotes: Generates GNU Make variable assignments by echoing command-substituted `crane digest` results, keeping images pinned by digest rather than tag.

nodes.name: latest-kind-images.sh
nodes.summary: Parses the kind GitHub release notes for a pinned kind version and regenerates make/kind_images.sh with KIND_IMAGE_K8S_* node image digest variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `curl | jq` with a named capture regex over the release body to extract digests, prefixed with the shared shell boilerplate header.

nodes.name: latest-kubebuilder-shas.sh
nodes.summary: Downloads kubebuilder-tools archives for each supported OS/architecture and prints their SHA256 checksums as KUBEBUILDER_TOOLS_*_SHA256SUM variables for make/tools.mk.
nodes.languageNotes: Validates a single version argument, then loops over bashing arrays while templating a multi-line output string with printf.

nodes.name: verify-chart-version.sh
nodes.summary: Lints a packaged cert-manager Helm chart tarball by extracting it to a temp directory and running chart-testing (ct lint) inside a pinned Docker image.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a mktemp directory with an EXIT trap for cleanup and allows the container runtime to be overridden via the DOCKER variable.

nodes.name: verify-errexit.sh
nodes.summary: Repository lint that scans shell scripts for `set -o errexit` (or an equivalent `set -e` form) and exits non-zero when any script lacks fail-fast behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Derived from Kubernetes tooling; detects scripts via a shebang grep and reports failures by conditionally creating a temp marker file.

nodes.name: verify-upgrade.sh
nodes.summary: End-to-end upgrade test that installs the last published cert-manager release in a kind cluster, upgrades to the current checkout via Helm and static manifests, verifies existing resources still work, then uninstalls.
nodes.languageNotes: Sources hack/build/version.sh for release discovery, overrides image tags in generated manifests with ytt, and polls `kubectl rollout status` until a bounded attempt limit.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide to cert-manager's GNU Make tooling, covering target documentation conventions, .PHONY usage, prerequisite types, and automatic tool provisioning.

nodes.name: cluster.sh
nodes.summary: Creates or validates a local kind cluster for development, selecting a pinned node image per Kubernetes version and patching CoreDNS for example.com test domains.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash script with dynamic flag-to-variable assignment via eval and bash process substitution for Corefile comparison.

nodes.name: help
nodes.summary: Prints usage, flags, and environment variables for the kind cluster script, then exits.

nodes.name: setup_kind
nodes.summary: Creates the kind cluster if absent, then verifies kube context, API responsiveness, Kubernetes version, and CoreDNS Corefile, failing with remediation hints.

nodes.name: e2e-ci.sh
nodes.summary: Thin CI wrapper that runs the end-to-end suite through Make with two flake attempts, CI mode enabled, and kind logs captured on exit.

nodes.name: e2e.sh
nodes.summary: Runs cert-manager's Ginkgo end-to-end suite against an existing kind cluster, translating environment variables into ginkgo flags and emitting JUnit artifacts.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: cert-manager adds Certificate and Issuer resource types to Kubernetes and automates obtaining, renewing, and using TLS certificates from ACME/Let's Encrypt, HashiCorp Vault, Venafi, or local in-cluster CAs. The README frames that purpose and the supported issuer backends, while the extensible-certificate-controller design record explains why the certificate controller was split into keymanager, requestmanager, and issuing components. Keep that pipeline in mind: the rest of the tour follows a Certificate from API object to signed Secret, then out to the deployed controller, webhook, and Helm chart.

tour.title: Controller Binary Bootstrap
tour.description: Every cert-manager component is a Go binary whose main function only handles logging, signal handling, and exit codes before delegating to a cobra command. In the primary controller, start.go loads and validates ControllerConfiguration and blank-imports the controller and issuer packages so their init functions register implementations, while app/controller.go builds the shared context, starts metrics, profiling and health servers, acquires leader election, and runs the enabled controllers. The options package defines the CLI flags and resolves the enabled controller set from configuration and feature gates.
tour.languageLesson: Go blank imports (`_ "some/package"`) execute a package's init functions without referencing any of its exported symbols. cert-manager relies on this to populate global controller and issuer registries before the binary starts, which keeps the wiring out of main.go.

tour.title: Core Kubernetes API Types
tour.description: The public API lives under pkg/apis and is the vocabulary every later component shares. types_certificate.go defines the Certificate spec and status, including SANs, renewal policy, the target Secret, keystores, and private key settings; types_certificaterequest.go defines the CSR hand-off object; and types_issuer.go defines Issuer, ClusterIssuer, and every backend configuration. generic_issuer.go contributes the GenericIssuer interface so controllers can treat namespaced and cluster-scoped issuers uniformly, while types.go holds shared constants such as label keys and default key usages.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces give cert-manager duck typing: any value implementing the GenericIssuer accessor methods can pass through the same controller code, so Issuer and ClusterIssuer do not need duplicated reconciliation logic.

tour.title: Defaulting, Conversion & Validation
tour.description: Kubernetes API conventions require an internal hub version alongside the versioned external types users submit. The internal certmanager/v1 package registers defaulting functions, such as the private key rotation policy, and generated conversions between internal and public v1 objects, while the validation package enforces rules for Certificates, Issuers, and CertificateRequests before a controller ever sees them. The ACME group receives the same treatment: its defaulting fills issuerRef kind and group on Order and Challenge objects when users omit them.
tour.languageLesson: In Kubernetes APIs the external version is the serialized contract, the internal version is the in-memory hub, and conversion-gen emits round-trip functions between them. Defaulting runs before validation, so validators can assume omitted optional fields already have sensible values.

tour.title: Generated Clients & Informers
tour.description: Controllers never call the API server for every read. The generated clientset wires typed clients for the certmanager.io and acme.cert-manager.io groups onto a shared REST configuration, the informer factory lazily builds and synchronizes shared caches for every resource, and listers provide read-only access to those caches. Apply configurations add fluent server-side-apply builders, which the controllers use to update specs and status without clobbering other field managers.
tour.languageLesson: A shared informer opens one watch per resource type and fans changes out to many handlers. Listers read from the local cache, which makes reconciliation cheap but eventually consistent, so controllers must tolerate briefly stale objects.

tour.title: Controller Runtime Framework
tour.description: All controllers share a single queueing framework built around the controller Context. Context carries the Kubernetes clients, informers, metrics, and ACME registries; controller.go provides the Run and worker loop with rate-limited workqueues and duration metrics; and register.go plus builder.go let each controller register a constructor that the runner instantiates by name. This is the glue that makes dozens of independent reconciliation loops behave like one coherent control plane.
tour.languageLesson: The workqueue pattern decouples event delivery from processing: event handlers enqueue object keys, a fixed pool of goroutine workers reconciles them, and rate limiting plus retries prevent one failing object from consuming the process.

tour.title: Certificate Reconciliation Pipeline
tour.description: A Certificate moves through several cooperating controllers rather than one monolith. The trigger controller compares the Certificate and its Secret against issuance policies and sets the Issuing condition; requestmanager creates, cleans up, and tracks CertificateRequests; keymanager creates and rotates the private key Secret; issuing drives issuance, validates the response, and updates status; and readiness evaluates the policy chain to set the Ready condition. This separation is exactly the design introduced in step 1 and lets each concern be reasoned about and tested independently.

tour.title: CertificateRequest & Issuer Backends
tour.description: Once a CertificateRequest exists, the generic certificaterequests controller owns the informers and workqueue but delegates signing to an issuer-specific implementation through the issuer Interface. Its shared sync routine validates approval and issuer state before invoking that backend, and the Factory resolves a GenericIssuer reference to a concrete implementation. The CA issuer is the simplest worked example: it signs requests with a key pair stored in a Secret, while SelfSigned, Vault, Venafi, and ACME all plug into the same contract.
tour.languageLesson: The issuer Interface is a classic Go strategy pattern: the controller depends only on Issue and Setup behavior, and each backend supplies its own implementation plus a factory registration, so adding Vault or Venafi requires no changes to the reconciliation loop.

tour.title: ACME Orders, Challenges & Solvers
tour.description: ACME is a multi-step protocol, so cert-manager models it as first-class Order and Challenge resources instead of hiding state in memory. The ACME order controller creates orders, tracks authorizations, creates challenges, finalizes orders, and stores the certificate, while the challenge controller schedules work and drives HTTP-01 or DNS-01 solvers. The DNS solver resolves provider configuration and credentials, and the lightweight acmesolver binary serves HTTP-01 tokens from inside the cluster.
tour.languageLesson: By persisting each protocol step as a Kubernetes object, cert-manager turns an external state machine into ordinary reconciliation. Progress survives controller restarts and operators can inspect Orders and Challenges with kubectl instead of reading logs.

tour.title: Admission Webhook & CA Injector
tour.description: The webhook binary protects the API surface described in step 3. The internal webhook package installs the API schemes and assembles an admission plugin chain, pkg/webhook/admission adapts those plugins to controller-runtime's validating and mutating webhooks with warnings and JSON patches, and the server package runs the secure listener with health, metrics, and graceful shutdown. cainjector solves the bootstrap trust problem by reading CA data from Secrets, kubeconfigs, or Certificates and injecting the resulting bundle into webhook configurations, APIServices, and CRD conversion webhooks.
tour.languageLesson: Admission plugins run as a chain: any plugin can reject a request or add warnings, and mutating plugins return JSON patches that Kubernetes applies before the object is persisted. This is how cert-manager enforces defaults beyond what CRD schemas can express.

tour.title: Helm Chart & Deployment
tour.description: The Helm chart is the supported installation path for everything built so far. values.yaml configures the controller, webhook, cainjector, ACME solver, startup API check, CRDs, RBAC, and monitoring, while values.schema.json validates user input before rendering. The controller Deployment wires replicas, leader election, feature gates, metrics, and security context, and the generated CRD manifests publish the Certificate schema from step 3. Containerfiles package each prebuilt binary into the shared base image.
tour.languageLesson: Helm merges values.yaml with user overrides and renders Go templates. CRDs are cluster-scoped API definitions with their own lifecycle, which is why the chart treats installing and upgrading them separately from the Deployment that runs the controller.

tour.title: Build, CI & Module Tooling
tour.description: The root Makefile is deliberately thin: it sets host and version variables and includes repository modules such as 00_mod.mk, which defines build flags, binary names, and chart paths. server.mk cross-compiles the controller, webhook, cainjector, acmesolver, and startupapicheck binaries for five Linux architectures, while go.mod pins the Kubernetes, controller-runtime, Vault, and Venafi dependencies for the main module. Scheduled workflows such as make-self-upgrade rerun generation and open a pull request when generated code drifts, keeping the clients and CRDs from steps 4 and 5 in sync.
tour.languageLesson: Make includes compose a build from small .mk fragments, and targets declare dependencies rather than scripts. Combined with Go modules, this gives cert-manager a reproducible way to build each binary from a pinned dependency set.
